segments.text: I was at a friend's house the other night, small get-together, nothing fancy. Just a few of us hanging out, music playing, snacks everywhere, everyone in a good mood. After a while, I went to use the bathroom, you know, quick and casual. In, out, back to the fun. Everything was fine, and so I went back to chatting, laughing, just enjoying the night. About 15 minutes later, someone else went in after me, and that's when my brain decided to panic. Wait, did I flush the toilet? My friend's in the middle of a story and I'm nodding along, but my head's somewhere else. I'm replaying everything, closing the door, washing my hands, checking my phone, and I just can't remember that part. I kept glancing toward the hallway, waiting for the sound of a flush like that would somehow clear my name. But it never came. The longer I waited, the worse it got. So I sat there, smiling, pretending everything was fine, while internally losing my mind. And then, just as I was about to lose it, the person came back, completely normal. No weird looks, no comments, nothing. So I guess I did flush, right? I mean, I must have. Still, for the rest of the night, I couldn't fully relax. I'd laugh at a joke with everyone else, but in the back of my head, I was still thinking, "What if I didn't?" There's no anxiety quite like the "Did I flush" kind. Harmless, invisible, and somehow powerful enough to mess with your peace of mind for hours.
